source_claim_original: 莫利范畴性定理：不可数范畴理论的特征
source_claim_translation: Morley's categoricity theorem: characterization of uncountably categorical theories.
canonical_statement: Let T be a first-order theory in a countable language. If T is categorical in one uncountable cardinal, then T is categorical in every uncountable cardinal.
domain_and_universes: A countable first-order language L; an L-theory T; infinite cardinals kappa and lambda. Exact Lean universes, cardinal representation, syntax, semantics, and model isomorphism APIs remain to be selected in the statement phase.
ordered_binders: a first-order language L with at most countably many symbols
the hypothesis that T is categorical in kappa
hypotheses: T is categorical in kappa, including existence of a model of cardinality kappa
conclusion: T is categorical in lambda for every uncountable cardinal lambda, including existence and uniqueness up to L-structure isomorphism at lambda.
statement_choices_requiring_source_audit: whether the primary source assumes T complete or obtains completeness from the categoricity convention
whether 'countable theory' means countable language, countable axiom set, or both
whether categoricity explicitly includes existence of a model in the cardinal
whether cardinality is expressed by exact cardinal equality or an equipotence witness

alternate_encodings.target: For all uncountable kappa and lambda, categoricity of T in kappa implies categoricity of T in lambda
alternate_encodings.relationship: equivalent after moving the existential source cardinal into universally quantified implication form

alternate_encodings.target: The spectrum of uncountable cardinals in which T is categorical is either empty or all uncountable cardinals
alternate_encodings.relationship: equivalent spectrum formulation under the same categoricity and existence conventions

excluded_degenerate_cases: Finite and countably infinite cardinals are outside the transfer conclusion. Uncountable languages, infinitary logics, non-elementary classes, and transfer from a cardinal where T has no model are excluded. The theorem does not assert that every countable theory is categorical anywhere.
foundation_profile: Lean 4 dependent type theory with a later explicit policy for classical choice, quotients, cardinal arithmetic, and model existence; no principle is credited at intake.
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel plus the repository-pinned mathlib environment; exact executable, imports, options, and transitive dependency closure remain open.
computation_profile: No computation, oracle, experiment, external theorem, or proof body is credited at intake.
formal_system: Lean 4 + pinned mathlib, pending selection or construction of first-order model-theory APIs.
source_revisions: Repository metadata and Morley's 1965 primary paper are identified in source-statement-crosswalk.md. Full-text capture, pinpoint premise mapping, errata review, immutable source hashing, and independent review remain open.
scope_nodes: MOR-DEF language, theory, model, cardinality, isomorphism, and categoricity definitions
MOR-SRC source convention alignment for countability, completeness, and existence
MOR-STRUCT structural analysis of models of an uncountably categorical theory
MOR-EXIST existence of models in every target uncountable cardinal
MOR-UNIQ uniqueness up to isomorphism in every target uncountable cardinal
MOR-TRANSFER recomposition for an arbitrary uncountable target cardinal
freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on changes to the countability scope, categoricity or model-existence convention, cardinal domain, source edition, Lean target, imports/toolchain, foundation/TCB policy, or rev-5.6 standard. Master acceptance is required before promotion.
status_boundary: This planned intake freezes the standard uncountable-categoricity transfer claim and its unresolved conventions. It does not elaborate a Lean proposition, accept source fidelity, establish a model-theory API, provide a proof body, or claim audit/theorem completion.
